first_impression.reaction: This is literally the argument James and I have had twice this month, so I clicked. The first line earns the scroll: 'Choosing between a Santorini or Mykonos wedding is a choice between two settings, not two standards.' No 'paradise', no 'dream day', and it doesn't pretend one island is objectively better. The takeaways go straight to ferries in wind and the CNI, which tells me someone has actually thought about guests and paperwork. Kept reading.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding: the short answer
journey.quote: Neither island wins. They answer different questions.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-offs over a listicle verdict. The cliff versus bare-feet-and-chapel framing is exactly how I'd explain it to Mum. I already know I'm leaning Santorini and James is leaning Mykonos, and now we have a way to talk about it.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.quote: Same figures for both: HNMS Naxos, the nearest listed station
journey.reaction: The table is the thing I'd send James, but two of its seven rows (season and legal) say the same thing in both columns. In an at-a-glance table that's wasted space; I skimmed past them looking for a difference that isn't there.

journey.quote: Andronis Luxury Suites in Oia has suites and villas perched on the cliffs, looking across the Aegean to the volcanic caldera, and is home to the two-Michelin-starred Lycabettus Restaurant.
journey.reaction: Welcome dinner, sorted in my head. This is the kind of detail that makes it feel like our wedding and not a resort package.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact, one person start to finish, and confirms each venue's inclusions in writing before you commit
journey.reaction: 'One person start to finish' answers my 'what does end-to-end actually mean' question better than most. Inclusions in writing speaks to the hidden-costs fear.

journey.quote: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: This is the insider detail I came for. Neither of us is Orthodox, so that's a chapel I'd have fallen for and then lost. 'Decide the ceremony before you fall for a chapel' is genuinely useful sequencing.

journey.quote: The Myconian Collection has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Half our guest list is international and a few have proper dietary needs. Good to know a venue can handle it properly rather than a sad side plate.

journey.quote: The island is synonymous with cosmopolitan, polished holidays, and the wedding settings follow: beach, bay, chapel and town.
journey.reaction: Everyone we know associates Mykonos with party season. The page dances around that. My parents will ask whether our wedding week ends up sharing the island with a beach-club crowd, and I can't answer from this.

journey.quote: Both islands have their own airport, and both airports sit within the Fraport Greece network.
journey.reaction: Who operates the airport means nothing to me or my guests. Skimmed.

journey.quote: In most cases passengers carry their own luggage up and down stairs, and some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities.
journey.reaction: This is my grandparents. Nobody else mentions the stairs. Exactly the sort of thing I'd forward to Dad, and it nudges me towards flying everyone in rather than ferrying.

journey.section: When to marry on each island
journey.quote: Choose your month by the ceremony time, the shade at your venue and how much buffer your guests have for travel, not by a single number in a table.
journey.reaction: Fair, and calm about the heat and wildfire points without scaremongering. I'd have liked the table to tell me more, but this is a sensible way to think about it.

journey.quote: Smartraveller also notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity near major destinations including Santorini, and advises following local authorities.
journey.reaction: Appreciate the honesty, but Mum will read 'volcanic activity near Santorini' and that's the end of Santorini for her. It's stated and then left there. I'm not asking for it to be hidden, just that it doesn't read as the last word.

journey.section: Getting legally married on either island, in brief
journey.quote: For the Greek civil steps on each island, check with the municipality and the Australian Embassy in Athens, including any fees.
journey.reaction: Lawyer brain: the Australian half is laid out well, then the Greek half is handed back to me as homework. 'Legal side sorted' is one of our top three goals. I don't even know from this whether a legal civil ceremony can happen at a hotel terrace or has to be at a town hall, which changes the whole venue shortlist.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos wedding questions, answered
journey.quote: The island matters less than the choices you make on it.
journey.reaction: No numbers, which I'd normally grumble about, but it's honest that guest count and venue drive cost more than the island, and it points to venues that publish packages. Acceptable for a comparison piece.

journey.quote: **You want a chapel above a beach.** Mykonos.
journey.reaction: The scenario list is the most useful bit for a couple who disagree. Each line has a real reason and named venues. Screenshot for James.

journey.section: Choose your island with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Paired with AUD quotes and someone in our time zone, this is the line that would actually get me to book a call. Not pushy.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a real Santorini or Mykonos wedding, with venue and date, that I can look at?
Can a legally binding civil ceremony be held at the hotel venues on each island, or only at the town hall?
On Mykonos, how does a wedding week sit alongside the party-season crowd, and are some bays quieter than others?
Which of these venues actually fit 60 to 90 guests, since the page doesn't say?
If a ferry is cancelled in wind, what happens to guests booked to arrive by sea the day before?
Has the seismic and volcanic note ever affected a wedding on Santorini, and how would we know if it might?

turn_offs_found.quote: Santo Wines sets the vows at the winery, with the caldera as witness against the setting sun.
turn_offs_found.why: 'The caldera as witness' is a little brochure-poetic, edging towards the 'say I do in paradise' tone I skim past. Mild, because the rest of the page is so plain and factual, but 'the winery holds ceremonies facing the caldera at sunset' says the same thing without the flourish.

would_share_with: James (partner): the short answer, the at-a-glance table and the 'Which island suits you' scenarios
Mum and Dad (contributing): the By sea section on stairs and luggage, and the heat, wildfire and wind section
James again: the Mykonos Grand Christian Orthodox rule and the legal section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start planning with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Soft and not hard-sell, and the fee-in-writing and one-person lines hit my biggest fears. The page also makes it obvious how many things need checking venue by venue, which is the case for handing it over. But I'd read another post or two and want to see a real wedding on one of these islands before I enquire.

top_3_changes: In 'Getting legally married on either island, in brief', replace the closing 'check with the municipality' with a plain sentence on whether a civil ceremony can be held at a hotel venue or only at the town hall on each island (or flag it clearly as a booking-checklist question), because that decides the venue shortlist.

In 'Mykonos: town, beaches and bays', add an honest line on how a wedding week sits alongside the island's party-season reputation (for example, which wedding bays are quieter), so parents' first objection is answered on the page.
In the at-a-glance table, merge the identical Season and Legal steps rows into one 'Same for both islands' line, so the table only shows the rows where the islands actually differ.
